hard-prohibition.name: Hard prohibitions
hard-prohibition.summary: A short list of actions the file states the agent must never take, without hedging.
hard-prohibition.detail: Stated as flat "never" rather than "prefer not to", and usually naming the exact action rather than a category. Several files pair the rule with what to do when a user asks anyway.

worked-examples.name: Good and bad pairs
worked-examples.summary: A style rule is shown with the wrong version beside the right one.
worked-examples.detail: Some files pair whole code blocks, others contrast inline within a sentence. The rule is stated once and then demonstrated twice, which removes the judgement call at the margins.

generated-file-guard.name: Generated file guards
generated-file-guard.summary: Generated files are named, along with the generator to run instead.
generated-file-guard.detail: The lists are explicit paths rather than a description of what generated files look like. Several entries also name the command and, in a few cases, the extra steps that have to happen in the same change, such as deleting a superseded fixture.

verification-matrix.name: Verification by change type
verification-matrix.summary: The kind of change is mapped to the specific checks that cover it.
verification-matrix.detail: A rendering change maps to one command, a protocol change to another. Several files also state what the default test command leaves out, which is otherwise discoverable only by finding the gap.

nested-instructions.name: Nested instruction files
nested-instructions.summary: Per-package AGENTS.md files, with a stated order of precedence.
nested-instructions.detail: The root file covers repository-wide navigation and defers subsystem detail to a file next to the code. Where the files could conflict, the precedence order is written down rather than left to the agent.

single-source.name: Pointing at the source of truth
single-source.summary: The file refuses to copy values that live somewhere authoritative.
single-source.detail: Version numbers, rule lists and counts are replaced with a pointer to the config, script or array that defines them. Some files state the reason directly: a copied value drifts from the thing it copied.

skill-routing.name: Router files
skill-routing.summary: The entry file dispatches to deeper task guides rather than containing them.
skill-routing.detail: A short index maps a kind of work to the guide to read before starting it. The deeper document is loaded when the task touches that subsystem, instead of on every request.

behavioral-conditioning.name: Behavioral framing
behavioral-conditioning.summary: Rules about how to approach the work rather than facts about the repository.
behavioral-conditioning.detail: Surface tradeoffs, do not over-build, touch only what was asked. Two files state outright that these sections were written from recurring mistakes in agent-authored changes to that repo.

house-vocabulary.name: House vocabulary
house-vocabulary.summary: Specific words the project does and does not use, defined once.
house-vocabulary.detail: Ranges from fixing the spelling of a domain term across all prose, to defining the difference between two near-synonyms, to listing individual words that may not appear. Naming drift is hard to catch in review, which is what these rules are aimed at.

architecture-narrative.name: Architecture as narrative
architecture-narrative.summary: How the system works, written out, rather than a list of rules about it.
architecture-narrative.detail: Request lifecycles, data flows and component boundaries. It lets the agent derive an answer for a case the file does not cover, at the cost of length.

ratchet.name: Ratchets
ratchet.summary: Baselines that may only shrink and lists that may only grow.
ratchet.detail: A known-violations file, a lint warning count, or a tombstone list, each with a direction of travel stated in the file and usually enforced in CI.

contribution-etiquette.name: Contribution etiquette
contribution-etiquette.summary: Rules for what the agent may open, push or post on the project's behalf.
contribution-etiquette.detail: Covers pull requests, issues, @-mentions and commit trailers. Two of these files give the reason as agent traffic specifically: unsolicited pull requests, and issues that attract duplicate work from other agents.

scope-layering.name: Scope layering
scope-layering.summary: Different rules for different actors, with a test for which set applies.
scope-layering.detail: One file covers maintainers, external contributors and forks, and states how the agent determines which it is before the rules take effect.

context-budget.name: Context budgeting
context-budget.summary: Rules governing what may enter the model context, with size caps.
context-budget.detail: Appears in repos that build agents. The context window is treated as a resource with an owner, a cap per item, and a review threshold.
